title: E-Depot
summary: The whole life of a container in a depot, from the order to the gate out, in one system.
alt: Container in/out screen: search results for a container number and a gate-in photo timeline for that container.

steps.label: the problem
steps.text: Every container going in or out of the depot was recorded by hand. The order, the gate, the inspection, the repair and the paperwork all lived on different sheets of paper.

steps.label: what i built
steps.text: One flow that follows the container through every stage, so each person on the floor picks it up where the last one left off.
facts: Each user only sees their own depots, shipping lines and menus — admin, surveyor, tally, QC and the roles around them.
Repair estimates are priced from the M&R tariff per shipping line, with damage photos attached.
Bulk storing orders come in from Excel; every container's photos download as one zip.

steps.label: what changed
steps.text: In and out are digital end to end, and the reports — stock, moves in and out, dwell time with monthly trends — come straight from the data. Dozens of people use it across six depots, each with its own staff and routine.

title: Global Super App
summary: One internal platform that runs a logistics group day to day: trucking, depot, warehouse, workshop, purchasing, finance and helpdesk, each as a module behind a single login.
note: internal system, used daily across several companies in the group. code is private.
role: Fullstack developer: maintains the platform, builds new modules and keeps it fast and reliable.
alt: Super App dashboard with HR announcements, safety bulletins, important forms and a purchase request approval table, next to the same approvals on a phone.

steps.label: what i inherited
steps.text: A large PHP platform already in production, built by another developer: nine modules, many databases, little documentation, and people depending on it every day. Some screens hung for seconds, uploads failed at random, and approvals sometimes never reached the approver.

steps.label: what i added
steps.text: New features built into the existing structure, so they feel like they were always there.

steps.label: what i fixed
steps.text: Problems traced to their cause instead of patched on the surface.
facts: Slow job completion in trucking came from blocking network calls; moved them out of the request, so the screen answers straight away.
Random upload failures were DNS failures to the file server; added fixed resolution and retries with time limits.
Notifications that silently never arrived now check the phone number first and log every failure.
An invoice numbering bug at the 1,000th item, and EDI files marked as sent before the email actually went out.

title: Business Agent
summary: Quotations, invoices and receivables for small businesses, with an AI agent that can read and change that data from chat or Telegram, and never changes anything without asking first.
note: personal project, built end to end. not in use by real customers yet.
role: Solo build: product design, backend, agent design and frontend.
alt: Agent Playground: the agent looks up a customer and products, shows a quotation summary and waits for approval; after the user says yes it creates the quotation. Same flow on a phone.

steps.label: the problem
steps.text: Small businesses keep quotations in Word, invoices in Excel and who still owes money in their head. An AI assistant could help, but one that can write to the books must never act on a misunderstanding.

steps.label: what i built
steps.text: A normal web app for customers, products, quotations, invoices and reports, plus an agent that uses the same business rules through a set of tools.
facts: Actions that change data are never run when the model asks for them. The backend stores them, shows a summary, and code — not the model — decides whether the next message is a yes.
If a reply mentions a quotation or invoice number that does not exist, the reply is held back instead of shown, so made-up documents never reach the user.

steps.label: around the agent
steps.text: The parts that make it usable day to day, not just in a demo.

title: Reminder app
summary: Reminders, WhatsApp delivery and document sign-off for Kalimantan Prima Persada.
note: client found through my own marketing. scoped with them face to face.
alt: Reminder app dashboard: counts of total, unread, pending and completed reminders, an urgent-items alert and a list of recent reminders.

steps.label: how it started
steps.text: A real freelance project I won through my own marketing — no agency, no platform in between. I met the Kalimantan Prima Persada team several times to understand how they work before writing any code.

steps.label: what i built
steps.text: A system that makes sure the right people get the right reminder — and actually see it.

features.title: Reminders
features.text: Sent to one person or a whole role, tracked from read to completed, with notes.

features.title: Schedules
features.text: Daily, weekly or monthly at a set time. A scheduler checks every minute and sends them on its own.

features.title: WhatsApp
features.text: Each reminder also lands on the recipient's WhatsApp, with a delivery log for the admin.

features.title: E-signature
features.text: Upload a PDF, then sign or reject it. The signature is stamped into the file itself.

steps.label: what they got
steps.text: A system shaped around their routine, not a template — recurring reminders that run without anyone pressing send, and sign-off that no longer needs paper.
